claims.rule: Suspect drug rash: generalised rash after new medication
Diagnose probable fixed drug eruption
claims.reason: Page precondition is 'following ingestion of a medication', not an existing drug-rash finding or possible diagnosis. The rule chains onto 'Suspect drug rash', which requires generalised rash within 3 months of a new medication; fixed drug eruption is localized spots and may follow any ingestion. Also ignores the 'No' branch (patient not on ART/TB meds/co-trimoxazole/TPT).
claims.fix: Use a medication-ingestion finding (or drop the precondition) instead of the drug eruption concept.

rules.rule: Suspect drug rash: generalised rash after new medication
rules.problem: Timing is tested on medication start, an approximation of 'rash appeared within 3 months of starting'.

Precondition is drug-rash finding/possible dx, which needs generalised rash plus new medication within 3 months; page only says following ingestion of a medication, localized spots. Probable is justified by 'likely'.

rules.rule: Urgent: drug rash with markers of severity
rules.problem: Urgent justified by box heading. Footnote 1 criteria for shock (pulse >=100, RR >30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) are not encoded; mouth/eye site concepts possibly broad.

summary: Most consequential: hyperpigmentation and macule (fixed drug eruption features from the non-urgent branch) are wrongly listed as markers of severity in the check_for task (c023, c024). The fixed drug eruption rule chains on the drug-rash suspicion rule, which does not match the page's 'following ingestion of a medication'. Mouth/eye finding-site concepts are possibly broader than mucosal involvement, and BP < 90/60 is split into SBP/DBP; otherwise the urgent rule is faithful.
